title: Physical activity and psychosocial characteristics of asymptomatic subjects and low back pain patients in real life (Subproject 5)
summary: Chronic low back pain is one of the most widespread health problems worldwide. However, the understanding, successful approaches to prevention and treatment of low back pain are still limited. This is partly due to the fact that fundamental associations between pain, psychosocial risk factors and resources, health behavior (i.e., physical activity), and the morphology and motion of the spine have rarely been studied together from an interdisciplinary perspective. In addition, previous research on low back pain has usually applied single occasion designs (e.g., magnetic resonance imaging or one-off questionnaire surveys) lacking relevance and not providing any insight into the everyday reality of individuals. To better understand chronic low back pain and back health, this subproject (in close collaboration with subproject 1 and subproject 4) will combine, for the first time, data on psychosocial factors (e.g., thoughts and feelings, self-regulation) and health behavior (physical activity, medication intake) in the natural environment of the individuals over longer periods of time in real time and evaluate them together with data on the morphology and motion of the spine. Individuals who take part in the study, both with and without back pain, will be asked about their physical activity, thoughts and feelings five times a day using a smartphone. Participants will also wear an accelerometer to assess physical activity throughout the day, at work and during leisure time. Data from ambulatory assessment will be analyzed together with data from the laboratory (e.g., data on the morphology and motion of the spine, questionnaire data). The primary outcome variable is the number of minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (leisure).

interventions.name: At baseline (T0), participants with chronic low back pain provide data on the following aspects: Occurrence of low back pain according to the time-based criterion of the past 12 weeks, age, gender, marital status, having children, education, employment status, income level, subjective social status

At baseline (T0) and follow-up (T2, T3) assessments, asymptomatic participants provide data on the same set of measures as participants with chronic low back pain, except for the PSEQ and the AE-FS. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Written inform consent
•	Individuals with chronic low back pain or asymptomatic individuals aged 18 to 64 years
•	Pain duration >12 weeks
•	Pain localization: lumbopelvic region
•	Indications for surgery: disc degeneration, facet joint arthrosis, spondylolisthesis
Exclusion criteria:
•	Professional, competitive, and top athletes
•	Acute infections
•	Abuse of addictive substances 
•	Pregnancy
•	BMI >28 kg/m2
•	Central or peripheral neurologic impairments (e.g., spinal cord injury, radicular symptoms, sensory deficits) 
•	Irritated, inflamed, and infected tissues in the measuring areas of the back
•	Spinal fractures
•	Osteoporosis
•	Tumor diseases and bone metastases
•	Previous spinal surgery
•	Strong drug therapy (opioids, muscle relaxants, antiepileptics)
•	Intake of long-acting antihistamines and/or systemic glucocorticoids and/or immunosuppressive drugs
•	Rheumatic diseases
•	Active systemic diseases (e.g., tuberculosis, collagenosis, multiple sclerosis, autoimmune diseases, acquired immune deficiency syndrome)
•	Internal diseases that pose a potential risk to the study participants during the measurements (e.g., coronary heart diseases) and/or influence the findings 
•	Malpositions or anomalies of the lower extremities
